source: GIZ (Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit), Support of Regional Economic Cooperation in Asia (SRECA), in cooperation with MAFF General Directorate of Agriculture — គោលការណ៍ណែនាំអំពីការនាំចេញផ្លែស្វាយស្រស់ពីប្រទេសកម្ពុជាទៅប្រទេសចិន (Guideline on Fresh Mango Export from Cambodia to China), Final Version, Phnom Penh, December 2020, 67pp
text:
Overview of the export market context for Cambodian mango, per the GIZ/SRECA fresh-mango-export-to-China guideline (Final Version, December 2020).

China is described as the world's largest producer, importer, and consumer of fresh fruit. Rapid Chinese economic growth pushed average urban annual income up sharply between 2009 and 2018 (the source cites a roughly two-and-a-half-fold increase over the decade), and Chinese consumers have more purchasing power and growing interest in health and food quality. Fresh fruit imports into China grew substantially over the 2009-2018 decade (the source cites growth from roughly USD 1.2 billion to over USD 6.9 billion in annual import value), with around 200 fruit types from 28 countries permitted for import as of 2019.

Cambodia grows mango (ស្វាយ, Mangifera indica) nationwide; the guideline lists numerous traditional/local Cambodian mango varieties by Khmer name (transliterated): Svay Kev Chin, Kev Lor Miet, Kev Sa Ry, Kev Lor Mut, Kev Pong Maon, Kev Moung, Kev Srouch, Kev Thlong, Kev Phum Sen, Kev Kbal Damrey, Svay Paom, Svay Yak, Svay Kiev Sang Ve, Kev La Hong, Kro Horm, Kev Leak, Svay Khtis Dong, and Svay Ma Kak.

For export purposes, Cambodia's General Directorate of Agriculture (GDA) tested a number of imported/grafted mango varieties over a multi-year trial and found the local climate and soil suitable for export-oriented varieties including: Guire #82, Tainon #1, R2E2, Keitt, Irwin, Shan Lin, Yuwin #6, Renong #1, Jinh Wang/Xishi, Red Golden Dragon, Narissus Mango, and Sensation. Of these, Keitt and R2E2 were already in commercial harvest at the time of writing, with R2E2 noted as a particularly popular variety for export because its harvest window falls when competing supply (including China's own domestic mango varieties and Thai mango) is lower — a comparative harvest-calendar chart in the source (by month) is used to illustrate this timing advantage.

The guideline also discusses competitiveness factors for Cambodian mango exports: (1) quality and origin trust — Chinese buyers reportedly still favour known grafted/imported varieties and traceable, certified orchards over generic local supply, though a trial shipment to the Guangzhou Jiangnan wholesale market was reported to have been well received; (2) fruit size and grading consistency — inconsistent sizing was flagged as a weakness Cambodian exporters need to address through better grading; and (3) reliable, large-volume supply and packaging that meets China's quarantine and packaging requirements.
caveat: This document is very likely the same GIZ/SRECA fresh-mango-export-to-China guideline series already represented as mango Source C in the knowledge base (processed in Batch 43), but this is a later, more complete edition (dated December 2020, 67pp, vs. the earlier-processed 53pp version with data through 2018).
